statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every finite vector s of 64-bit integers, the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(r) and cnt(r[i], x) = cnt(s, x) for every integer x is exactly 1 if cnt(s, x) <= cnt(nums, x) for every integer x, and is exactly 0 otherwise. Here cnt(a, x) is the number of positions j in a with a[j] = x. Thus the entries of r, identified up to permutation of their elements, are precisely all distinct sub-multisets of nums, each occurring once, and the outer order of entries in r is arbitrary.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 10 and -10 <= nums[i] <= 10 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail by overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 10 and -10 <= nums[i] <= 10 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = product over v in D of (cnt(nums, v) + 1), where D is the finite set of distinct integers occurring in nums and cnt(nums, v) is the number of indices j with nums[j] = v. Equivalently, len(r) is the number of distinct sub-multisets of nums.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 10 and -10 <= nums[i] <= 10 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(r) and every integer x, cnt(r[i], x) <= cnt(nums, x), where cnt(a, x) is the number of occurrences of x in a. In particular, every returned vector is a sub-multiset of nums and contains no value more times than nums does.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 10 and -10 <= nums[i] <= 10 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for all i and j with 0 <= i < len(r) and 0 <= j < len(r), if cnt(r[i], x) = cnt(r[j], x) for every integer x, then i = j. Thus no two entries of r represent the same subset, even after reordering their elements.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 10 and -10 <= nums[i] <= 10 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every finite vector s of 64-bit integers satisfying cnt(s, x) <= cnt(nums, x) for every integer x, there exists i with 0 <= i < len(r) such that cnt(r[i], x) = cnt(s, x) for every integer x. Thus every sub-multiset of nums is represented among the entries of r.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 10 and -10 <= nums[i] <= 10 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 1 <= len(r) <= 2^len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(r), 0 <= len(r[i]) <= len(nums).
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 10 and -10 <= nums[i] <= 10 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there is exactly one index i with 0 <= i < len(r) such that len(r[i]) = 0, namely the empty subset.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 10 and -10 <= nums[i] <= 10 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there is exactly one index i with 0 <= i < len(r) such that cnt(r[i], x) = cnt(nums, x) for every integer x, namely the subset containing the whole multiset nums.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 10 and -10 <= nums[i] <= 10 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer v with cnt(nums, v) > 0, there is exactly one index i with 0 <= i < len(r) such that len(r[i]) = 1 and r[i][0] = v.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 10 and -10 <= nums[i] <= 10 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer k with 0 <= k <= len(nums), there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(r) such that len(r[i]) = k.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 10 and -10 <= nums[i] <= 10 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer v and every integer k with 0 <= k <= cnt(nums, v), the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(r) and cnt(r[i], v) = k is exactly the product over u in D with u != v of (cnt(nums, u) + 1), where D is the set of distinct integers occurring in nums. An empty product is 1. In particular, for each value v present in nums and each possible multiplicity k of v, there is one returned subset for every choice of multiplicities of the other values.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 10 and -10 <= nums[i] <= 10 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r for nums and a result r' for nums', for every i with 0 <= i < len(r) there exists j with 0 <= j < len(r') such that cnt(r[i], x) = cnt(r'[j], x) for every integer x; and for every j with 0 <= j < len(r') there exists i with 0 <= i < len(r) satisfying the same equality. Consequently len(r) = len(r').
preconditions: nums and nums' are slices of 64-bit integers, each with length between 1 and 10 and all entries in [-10, 10], and cnt(nums', x) = cnt(nums, x) for every integer x, so nums' is a permutation of nums.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer v, the sum over i with 0 <= i < len(r) of cnt(r[i], v) equals (c * (c + 1) / 2) * product over u in D with u != v of (cnt(nums, u) + 1), where c = cnt(nums, v) and D is the set of distinct integers occurring in nums. Here the product is over all u in D except v, and an empty product is 1. In particular, if v is not in nums, this sum is 0.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 10 and -10 <= nums[i] <= 10 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).
